title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Sloane73 Q2 separates dung source, cold-air condenser, water product, and solar exposure branch
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the retained complete Sloane73 Book I Q2 source, a vessel of distillation sits within prepared horse dung while its head remains in cold air; the ascending material turns to water through the air's coldness, falls, and rises again. The same passage then gives another method: the same vessel is exposed to strong summer sunlight for night and day. Keep dung/source, vessel, cold-air condition, water product, and alternate solar exposure distinct; the source does not explicitly state the alternate branch's output.

source_evidence.quote: þat, þat þing þat bi vertu of þe fier of þe doung þat ascendith þerby be turned into watir *by vertu of cooldnes of þe eir and falle doun aȝen and ascende vp aȝen. and þus ȝe haue fier wiþoute fier, and but wiþ litil traueile.

supporting_source_evidence.quote: Also anoþer maner of fier. sette ȝoure vessel forseid to þe strong reuerberacioun of þe sunne in somer tyme, and lete it stonde þere nyȝt and day.

whole_source.owner: Sloane73 c1460–70, Book I p6 / editorial folio 13v, Q2_REAL_SUN_HEAT; complete local passage with both procedures
whole_source.layer: Furnivall edition; retained source transcription, not a new manuscript collation.
